sections.heading: What is a JSON file?
body: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is an open text format that stores data as nested key-value pairs. Humans can read it, machines can process it reliably.
For ORIF, we use Schema.org's event vocabulary and add theatre-specific categories based on the recommendations of the Integrated Authority File (GND).

sections.heading: From programme to interface
body: Theatres usually publish their programmes through CMS, planning or ticketing systems. The web agency or in-house IT team maps the backend fields to the ORIF data model once.
The programme is then also provided as a machine-readable JSON link. The visible website remains unchanged, while platforms, archives and other services can retrieve the data automatically.

sections.heading: The ORIF interface
body: The Open Repertoire Interchange Format (ORIF) builds on Schema.org so event data can be captured and exchanged consistently. The goal is an open, licence-free standard aligned with the needs of cultural practitioners.
ORIF distinguishes between creative work data and event data: production team, source material and descriptions on one side; venue, date, ticket information and daily cast on the other.

sections.heading: What is a connector?
body: A connector is the software bridge between a theatre system and the Cultural Data Space. It handles authentication, data format validation and the transfer protocol.
We provide reference connectors for common systems and document the protocol for in-house implementations.

sections.heading: Sending and receiving via the data space
body: The Cultural Data Space acts as a broker: data senders (theatres) and data recipients (platforms, archives) meet here on the basis of agreed standards.
Every sender decides who may use which data - theatres remain in control.

sections.heading: Documentation & examples
body: Schema.org Event docs, technical specification on GitHub and on the Academy Dortmund website.
Application examples: Stadttheater Augsburg, Theaterstücke FRECARO.
